ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$ and $D$ lie on the circle $\odot O$, and $BC$ is a diameter. If $\angle ADC=30^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle OCA$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AB, as shown in the figure,\\
since BC is a diameter,\\
hence $\angle BAC=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle B=\angle ADC=30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACB=90^\circ-\angle B=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
that is, $\angle OCA=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

Segment BC is drawn horizontally across the circle through O, so BC is a diameter, with B on the left side and C on the right side. Point A is on the upper-right part of the circle, point D is on the lower-right part of the circle, and chords AC, DC, and AD are drawn. The given angle is ∠ADC = 30°. Reasoning: Add the auxiliary chord AB. Since BC is a diameter, the inscribed angle subtending BC is a right angle, so ∠BAC = 90°. Angles ABC and ADC both subtend the same chord AC, so ∠ABC = ∠ADC = 30°. In triangle ABC, ∠ACB = 180° - 90° - 30° = 60°. Since O lies on BC, ray CO is the same direction as ray CB, so ∠OCA = ∠BCA = 60°.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: A, C, and D are points on the same circle, with O as center and C at the right end of diameter BC; the angle ADC is an inscribed angle whose sides pass through A and C. Read from the text that angle ADC is 30 degrees and BC is a diameter of circle O, so C is on the circle and O is the center. The inscribed angle ADC intercepts arc AC not containing D, so the measure of that arc, and equivalently central angle AOC, is 2 × 30 = 60 degrees.
